subjects.note: Streets the city stopped being a street — vacated for a building or a park.
Cutting streets to their official level and surfacing them.
Branch libraries — several of them shops the city rented one year at a time.
Rail lines run into factories and yards — the industrial city, mostly gone by 1930.
Until about 1930 the Board voted on whether you could keep animals at your address.

summary: In 1914 M. Bohnert was licensed to keep three horses and a cow behind 214 Chenery Street. For twenty years after that the Board was grading and paving this valley street by street — Chenery, Diamond, Surrey, Sussex — and through the 1920s it was selling off the buildings standing in the way of the Bernal Cut. In 1964 the neighbourhood's branch library was a room the city rented from Antonio Pardini at 2909 Diamond Street, for $200 a month.
